committee: CC City Council Meeting of the Whole
overview: The Medford City Council Committee of the Whole convenes the full council membership to conduct preliminary hearings, review departmental operations, and deliberate on municipal policies and proposals prior to formal action by the regular City Council. Across the 49 meetings recorded between May 21, 2024, and October 13, 2026, the committee focused extensively on multi-session departmental budget reviews, federal and local grant allocations, and proposed regulatory ordinances. The body also manages administrative responsibilities including council leadership selection, charter review amendments, municipal staff recruitment, and land use planning. At its most recent recorded meeting on October 13, 2026, the committee entered an executive session to discuss litigation strategy regarding Alua et al. v. City of Medford et al. before adjourning.

threads.name: Municipal operating budget reviews
threads.summary: The committee conducts extended rounds of preliminary departmental budget hearings each spring prior to final council action. In 2024, it held preliminary sessions examining the FY25 school, health, and planning department requests (M01). For FY26, the committee established eight shared budget priorities, debated structural deficits, free cash reserves, and departmental requests across several weeks, and reviewed the mayor's proposed operating budget (M12#1, M15#1, M17#6, M20#4). For FY27, councilors assembled budget recommendations and conducted seven rounds of preliminary departmental reviews covering public works, fire, library, and school operations before Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn presented the operating budget overview (M29#1, M33#1, M40#3, M43#1).

threads.name: Community Preservation Act funding recommendations
threads.summary: The committee reviews annual project appropriation recommendations submitted by the Community Preservation Committee. In January 2025, CPA Manager Theresa Dupont presented eight FY25 funding proposals totaling over $1.8 million across housing, recreation, and historic preservation, all of which the committee referred to the regular council meeting (M09#1, M09#2, M09#3). In January 2026, the committee reviewed eleven FY26 funding proposals totaling approximately $2.4 million, including requests for the Medford Affordable Housing Trust, sports field lighting, and historic cemetery preservation (M26#1, M26#10). The committee voted to refer the entire FY26 funding package favorably to the regular City Council meeting (M26#13).

threads.name: Community Development Block Grant action plans
threads.summary: The committee evaluates annual Community Development Block Grant action plans and hears funding requests from non-profit service providers and city departments. In April 2025, Grants Manager Laurel Siegel presented an estimated $1.384 million plan for housing loans, business grants, and public services, which the committee referred for a full council public hearing (M14#1, M14#3). In April 2026, Siegel presented the Program Year 52 allocation under the FY27 action plan totaling approximately $1.733 million in federal funds (M34#1). Following presentations from public service organizations seeking funds for elder nutrition, housing advocacy, and language programs, the committee referred the plan to the regular meeting for final approval (M34#3, M34#6, M34#11).

threads.name: Tree canopy and preservation ordinances
threads.summary: The committee has worked on several regulatory drafts intended to protect and expand Medford's tree canopy. In November 2024, the committee reviewed three ordinances establishing a Tree Committee, updating public shade tree rules, and addressing trees on private property, referring the drafts to city staff and a working group (M05#1, M05#2). In July 2025, the committee approved and referred an amended Tree Committee Ordinance to the regular City Council (M22#1). In July 2026, Councilor Callahan introduced the Public Tree Ordinance, and following amendments regarding resident notification and discussion of unauthorized removal fines, the committee voted to refer the amended paper to the regular meeting with outstanding questions for staff (M46#1).

threads.name: Standard compensation ordinance
threads.summary: The committee deliberated on proposed amendments establishing wage, benefit, and worker retention standards for city-contracted janitorial and security services. After tabling the paper in January 2026 and keeping it in committee in February to allow the administration and procurement department to review legal and operational implications (M25#2, M27#1), the council debated competing drafts from city legal counsel and council leadership in April 2026 (M32#1). Members also requested a written policy defining how councilors may access legal advice following disputes over attorney-client privilege (M32#2). The committee subsequently approved a motion reporting the updated redlined ordinance to the regular City Council session for final consideration (M32#4).

threads.name: City Clerk recruitment and appointment
threads.summary: Following a vacancy in the City Clerk office, the committee voted in January 2026 to repost the position without minimum requirements to widen the candidate pool (M25#3). During the May 2026 budget review, the clerk's office reported ongoing operational strains caused by staffing shortages while addressing vault storage and digital filing needs (M36#3). In June 2026, the committee conducted public interviews with finalists Kevin Foley and Laurel Siegel (M45#1). The committee approved a motion recommending and offering the City Clerk appointment to Laurel Siegel and recognized Acting Clerk Rich Eliseo for his service (M45#1).

threads.name: Zoning reform and land development studies
threads.summary: The committee tracks zoning revisions and redevelopment studies for commercial corridors and neighborhood squares. Committee updates in 2024 detailed progress on comprehensive zoning reform with consultant Innes Associates, corridor reviews for Mystic Avenue and Salem Street, and green score proposals (M02#3, M07#4). In November 2025, the committee reviewed a proposal to ground-lease three municipal parking lots in Medford Square for mixed-use development (M23#1). In 2026, the body received a planning presentation on the Wellington Transformation Study (M39#1), discussed draft recommendations from an Affordable Housing Linkage Nexus Study (M47#1), and authorized Planning Director Alicia Hunt to advance an RFP for a zoning consultant for the next phase of the Zoning Updates Project (M48#1).

threads.name: Executive sessions on litigation strategy
threads.summary: The committee periodically convenes in closed executive sessions under state law to discuss legal strategy when open sessions could compromise the city's position. In June 2025, the council voted to enter executive session regarding Aleesha Nunley Benjamin v. City of Medford (M21#1). In 2026, the body entered closed sessions regarding Chertog v. City of Medford in March (M28#2), an unspecified litigation matter following a DPW snowstorm review in April (M30#1, M30#2), and Turtog v. City of Medford et al. in May (M39#2). In October 2026, the committee again entered executive session to discuss strategy in Alua et al. v. City of Medford et al. and adjourned directly from the closed session (M49#1).
